chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa; and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — all of them from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara who said:

Zurara said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had obligated of the salat. He said: Five prayers during the night and the day. I said: Has He named them and clarified them in His Book? He said: Yes.

Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Establish prayer from the declining of the sun to the darkness of the night' [17:78]. The declining of the sun is its zenith-passing; so between the declining of the sun and the darkness of the night are four prayers — Allah named them, clarified them, and fixed their times. The darkness of the night is its midpoint.
Then He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: [17:78] '...and the recitation of dawn; indeed the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.' That is the fifth.

Allah the Exalted also said regarding this: [11:114] 'Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night' — and its two ends are the Maghrib and the morning, and the early hours of the night is the last 'Isha prayer.

And the Exalted said: [2:238] 'Guard your prayers and the middle prayer' — and it is the Zuhr prayer, and it is the first prayer that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed, and it is the middle of the day and the middle of the two daytime prayers, which are the morning prayer and the 'Asr prayer.
And in some recitations: [2:238] 'Guard your prayers and the middle prayer — the 'Asr prayer — and stand before Allah in devout obedience.'

He said: This verse was revealed on a Friday while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on a journey. The Messenger of Allah performed it (the Jumu'a prayer) and left it upon its condition during both travel and residence, and added two rak'at for the resident.

The two rak'at which the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) added on Friday for the resident were in place of the two sermons with the Imam. Therefore, whoever prays on Friday without a congregation should pray it as four rak'at, like the Zuhr prayer on other days.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ الْوُسْطَى: The middle prayer — identified by the Imam as Zuhr, the first prayer the Prophet prayed
key_terms.دُلُوكُ الشَّمْسِ: Declining/zenith of the sun — the moment when the sun passes its highest point (zawal), marking the start of Zuhr time
key_terms.غَسَقُ اللَّيْلِ: Darkness of the night — its midpoint (midnight), marking the latest time for 'Isha
key_terms.قَانِتِينَ: In devout obedience/standing humbly — describes the state of worshippers before God in prayer
key_terms.قُرْآنُ الْفَجْرِ: The recitation of dawn — the Fajr prayer, named so in Quran 17:78

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for the five daily prayers according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Zurara narrates his dialogue with Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) in which the Imam provides a detailed Quranic basis for the five obligatory daily prayers, identifying each prayer's time from Quran 17:78, 11:114, and 2:238. The Imam explains that the 'middle prayer' in Quran 2:238 refers to Zuhr, not 'Asr, while acknowledging a variant Quranic reading that names 'Asr. He then rules that whoever cannot attend Friday Jumu'a congregation should pray four rak'at of Zuhr, since the two extra rak'at of Jumu'a substitute for the two sermons with the Imam.
